day_shape: US-Iran war footing dominates: CENTCOM confirms Sirik wedding strike inquiry with 4 reported dead, Trump weighs declaring conflict over while extending Mideast deployments, IRGC claims 31st 'Saaeqah' phase hit US bases in UAE/Kuwait, one UK Parliament FCDO question tabled.

threads.label: Sirik wedding strike fallout
threads.summary: CENTCOM said it was investigating Iranian state-media reports that a US strike on Sirik killed four at a wedding, denying it targets civilians. IRIB and Defa Press claimed remnants showed a US F-18-delivered guided winged bomb, and Iran's UN mission wrote to the Security Council calling it a war crime.

threads.label: Trump weighs winding down Iran war
threads.summary: The Wall Street Journal and Jerusalem Post reported Trump is holding private meetings on declaring the Iran conflict over while extending Middle East deployments, with aides pushing to avoid pre-midterm escalation. Reuters separately reported senior White House officials will consider intensifying strikes after the 3 November midterms.

threads.label: Iranian retaliation claims and Hormuz posture
threads.summary: Defa Press claimed a 31st 'Saaeqah' operation targeted US bases in the UAE and Kuwait with missiles and drones, and reported Ansarallah fired 14 ballistic missiles at Saudi positions near al-Mokha. IRIB quoted parliamentary security chair Ibrahim Azizi saying the Strait of Hormuz 'lock' will not open without Iran's will, while Kayhan urged severing Persian Gulf fibre-optic cables.

threads.label: US economic pressure and shadow banking
threads.summary: Jerusalem Post reported Treasury Secretary Bessent said mounting allied economic isolation could force Tehran to a deal, with Trump administration officials openly discussing an internal uprising scenario. An Iran International investigation found Tehran uses more than a dozen banks in China and the UAE beyond last month's US-sanctioned network; IRIB cited China's Commerce Ministry opposing Iran sanctions.

threads.label: Gaza ceasefire enforcement and tunnels
threads.summary: The IDF said it killed a Palestinian who crossed the 'Yellow Line' in northern Gaza in an airstrike, and reported dismantling a roughly 1km tunnel, bringing tunnels demolished east of the Yellow Line since the October 2025 ceasefire to over 26km. Netanyahu pledged during a Gaza outpost visit with Chief of Staff Zamir to continue disarming Hamas.

threads.label: Iran internal repression and unrest
threads.summary: Iran International reported a 31-year-old protester wounded in Shahroud demonstrations was killed outside his family home by security forces, and said Tehran is preparing repression as economic anger builds. Thousands responded to Trump's query on an Iranian uprising citing fear and insufficient outside support; exiled Crown Prince Reza Pahlavi plans an Australia visit to press for embassy closure.

threads.label: Iran military-technology cooperation reports
threads.summary: The Financial Times reported Russia has been helping Iran develop supersonic cruise missiles, and NBC News reported Iranian hackers targeted US water, telecommunications and energy infrastructure in recent weeks. Global News reported Canada awarded over $2 million in contracts to the son of a former Iranian vice president despite a sanctions-evasion probe.
